title: Engineering Antiviral Agents via Surface Plasmon Resonance
protocol: Obtain the gene construct for each CVN2 variant and CVN2L0 protein in pET27b(+) vector from commercial sources.
Dissolve lyophilized plasmid DNA in sterile deionized distilled water to a final concentration of 100 ng/μl.
Dissolve peptone, yeast extract, and NaCl in ddH2O to prepare LB-Lennox culture medium.
Adjust the pH of the culture medium to 7.4.
Transform competent E. coli BL21 (DE3) with each variant (V2-V5) using a chemical method.
Split the transformation solution into 900 µL and 100 µL portions.
Transfer 100 µL onto LB-agar plates containing 50 µg/mL kanamycin.
Use a sterile cell spreader to evenly distribute the solution on the agar plate.
Incubate the agar plates overnight at 37 °C.
Subclone the CV-N gene into the NdeI and BamHI sites of pET11a for transformation using electrocompetent cells.
Generate mutations in CVN2L0 template gene containing two distinguished DNA sequences using a site-directed mutagenesis kit.
Use specific mutagenic primers to perform PCR for generating CVN2L029 and mutant CVN-E41A.
Start a series of sample reactions with varying concentrations of dsDNA templates (5-50 ng).
Add 1 µL of Dpn I restriction enzyme below the mineral oil overlay.
Thoroughly and gently mix reactions.
Spin down reactions in a table-top microcentrifuge for 1 min.
Incubate reactions at 37 °C for 1 h.
Thaw XL1-Blue supercompetent cells gently on ice.
Aliquot 50 µL of supercompetent cells to prechilled polypropylene round-bottom tubes.
Transfer 1 µL of Dpn I-treated single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) from each reaction to the aliquots of supercompetent cells.
Swirl transformation reactions carefully to mix.
Incubate transformations on ice for 30 min.
Remove any remaining mineral oil from pipette tip before transferring DNA.
Optionally, check transformation efficiency by mixing 1 µL of pUC18 control plasmid with 50 µL aliquot of supercompetent cells.
Apply heat pulse to the transformation reactions at 42 °C for 45 s.
Place reactions on ice for 2 min after heat pulse.
Add 0.5 mL of NZY+ broth to the transformation reactions and incubate at 37°C with shaking at 225-250 rpm for 1 h.
Plate 5 μL from control plasmid transformation on LB-ampicillin agar plates containing X-gal and IPTG.
Plate 250 μL from sample transformation on LB-ampicillin agar plates containing X-gal and IPTG.
Inoculate 50 mL of the cell cultures with a single colony of transformed E. coli cells to purify mutated plasmid DNA for analyses.
Inoculate a small amount of LB (containing ampicillin) with a single colony from the transformed plate for large-scale culture.
Using the overnight culture, inoculate the expression culture with 10 mM MgCl2, 10 mM MgSO4, and 20 mM glucose, diluting to 1/100.
Grow cells with vigorous shaking at 37 °C.
Cool the cells to 20 °C when the Abs 600 nm reaches between 0.4-0.6 (mid-log phase).
Induce cell growth with 1 mM IPTG and incubate overnight.
Centrifuge cells at 4,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C to harvest.
Discard the supernatant using a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in PBS buffer and centrifuge again at 4,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant with a pipette.
Resuspend the remaining pellet in 10 mL of lysis buffer and incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Subject the mixture to two freeze-thaw cycles (-80 °C).
Centrifuge the suspension at 4,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C to separate soluble and insoluble fractions.
Analyze the soluble and insoluble fractions using SDS-PAGE.
Purify proteins using Ni-NTA column chromatography.
Load the soluble fraction onto a regenerated Ni-NTA bead column (1 mL/min).
Wash the system with TBS buffer before starting a gradient (0-100% 500 mM imidazole in TBS over 60 min) and collecting fractions (1 mL/min).
Dialyze the purified proteins for biochemical characterization against 100 mM PBS.
Use His-Select Ni2+ affinity gel to bind and re-suspend his-tagged recombinantly expressed CV-N in buffer solutions with 20 mM imidazole and 250 mM imidazole, respectively.
Incubate in batch for at least 30 min.
Apply semi-purified proteins to a single-use prepacked column for buffer exchange and cleanup of biological samples.
Transfer protein solutions to centrifugation tubes with a 10 kDa cut-off filter.
Concentrate the protein solutions by centrifuging for 10 min at 4,500 x g and 4 °C.
Exchange analyte solutions to 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM sodium chloride, 3 mM EDTA, and 0.05% Tween20, pH 7.4 (HBS-EP(+)).
Add SPR running buffer to a dilution factor of 1:10.
Centrifuge the analyte solutions four times for 10 min at 4,500 x g and 4 °C.
Determine the protein concentration at 280 nm using a NanoDrop UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Use PBS (100 mM, pH 7.0) or SPR buffer as a blank.
Measure the protein concentration at three dilution steps: 1:1, 1:10, and 1:100.
Turn on the Dual Channel SPR system instrument, degasser, auto-sampler, and pump.
Wash the entire system with ddH2O for 1 hour.
Place ready-to-use running buffer HBS-EP(+) in a separate bottle.
Drop emersion oil onto the detector.
Mount a glass sensor chip coated with carboxymethyldextran hydrogel on the upper side, directly onto the detector below the three-port flow cell.
Open a run table by clicking on Form in the menu bar and Run Table Editor in the integrated SPRAutoLink software.
Choose BASIC_Immobilization from the list of available run tables.
Follow the steps of the experimental procedure on the computer screen.
Click on Sample Set Editor in the Form section to fill out the reagents list.
Click on Autosampler Direct Control as a "Tool" in the menu bar.
Choose 4 °C as the operating temperature.
Select SPR Instrument Direct Control via the corresponding tool.
Select Pump Direct Control via the corresponding tool.
Start the pump to infuse ddH2O by clicking Start.
Record data by clicking on SPR Instrument Direct Control and selecting Start.
Put coupling reagents in 300 μL vials.
Place the vials into the autosampler racks.
Start the run table by clicking on Run.
Use CMD500D chip to generate a micro-refractive index units (µRIU) = 2500 - 3000 flow cell with immobilized HA and µRIU = 400 flow cell with spike protein.
Refill pump refill at 25,000 µL/min.
Perform baseline adjustment for 30 s.
Inject 90 µL of sample activation solution (EDC/NHS) over 6 min contact time.
Hold for another 5 min after injection.
Repeat the cycle after baseline running for 1 min at 10 µL/min on only the left flow cell to inject and immobilize chemically synthesized peptides, HA, and spike protein at 20 µg/mL.
Allow for subsequent baseline adjustment with ddH2O for 1.5 min before quenching the activated chip surface with 1 M ethanolamine HCl pH 8.5.
Switch the tubes from the liquid sampler to the degasser from ddH2O into the bottle with HBS-EP(+).
Analyze the SPR sensorgrams.
Use various analyte concentrations (10-5 to 10-8 M) for kinetic studies.
Perform a regeneration step after each injection.
Measure blanks after different analytes.
Change the flow rate to 10 µL/min.
Start injections for a contact time of 4 min.
Generate a baseline for 5 min after each injection.
Include two regeneration steps of 2 min each with an interval of 30 s.
Inject buffer solution for blank measurements.
Subtract sensorgrams from sample runs to normalize protein concentrations.
Switch to "Post-Processing" mode in the software.
Select binding curves generated over time for each flow cell.
Export the overlay as a scrubber file (.ovr).
Align left and right curves to obtain response curves.
Subtract signals of the second reference channel from those of the ligand channel.
Clean fluidics with 50-100 mM glycine buffer pH 9.5 before and after measurements.
Rinse with water followed by 20% ethanol for thorough cleaning.
Use a more stringent clean with 0.5% SDS and glycine if necessary.
